title: Randomized controlled intervention study on the influence of an acute nutritional intervention on climate-related decision-making as an experimentally operationalized sub-aspect of individual climate resilience
summary:
Climate change represents one of the greatest challenges of our time. Diet, as a central aspect of daily life, not only has significant impacts on human health but is also a major driver of global environmental change. A plant-based diet, such as the Planetary Health Diet, has the potential to contribute to mitigating the climate crisis through its favorable CO₂ footprint while simultaneously preventing the development of chronic diseases. Moreover, there is initial evidence that diet can also influence human decision-making behavior.

This pilot study investigates for the first time, using a randomized controlled design, whether an acute dietary intervention in the form of a one-time breakfast, based on the principles of the “Planetary Health Diet,” can influence short-term decision-making in climate-related situations compared to a Western-diet-like breakfast. Should relevant effects be observed, larger follow-up studies could be designed to systematically examine the potential influence of diet on climate resilience and to evaluate the potential of diet-based interventions to promote health and societal adaptability to climate change.

As secondary endpoints, differences in neurotransmitter and amino acid profiles in blood and urine will be assessed, and possible associations between these biological markers and decision-making behavior will be analyzed. All examinations involve only minimal burden for participants.
conditions: climate-related decision-making as a preventive measure

interventions.name: High-carbohydrate, low-fiber, low-protein breakfast (one-time), 3 days of dietary documentation using an app

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Students of the University of Augsburg
Willingness to consume a prescribed breakfast
Willingness to use the dietary app “LogMeal”
Ability to participate in the experimental tasks
Sufficient knowledge of German to understand the study instructions
Exclusion criteria:
Acute or chronic diseases requiring a special diet, including Type I diabetes
Eating disorders or restrictive dietary patterns
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Allergies or intolerances to components of the provided breakfast meals
Psychiatric diagnoses or cognitive impairments
Use of antidepressants, antipsychotics, or ADHD medication
Nicotine abuse
Alcohol or drug use (including cannabis) during the study
Obesity, defined as BMI > 30 kg/m²
Use of antibiotics within three months prior to the start of the study
Use of pre- or probiotics during the study period
